title: Saving 80,000 Gold in Another World for my Retirement
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Mitsuha, an orphaned eighteen-year-old who looks like a child, falls from a cliff and finds she can travel between modern Japan and a medieval fantasy world. She sells modern goods, wins a place with a local lord, opens a shop in the capital and trains with mercenaries on Earth while building toward a retirement fund of 80,000 gold coins.
life_message: Security comes from shrewd planning, hard work and using one's advantages, while still protecting the people one comes to care about.

content.note: AniList tags War, Guns and Military-style conflict; ANN notes mercenary training and drift toward arms dealing. Graphic detail not confirmed (to verify).
Near death from a cliff fall and wolves (publisher blurb); grief over dead family (ANN).
MangaUpdates lists a Loli protagonist tag; ANN's reviewer is critical of the genre's focus on childlike heroines. No sexual content reported.
Mitsuha represses grief and hears her late brother's imagined voice (ANN).
Arms dealing, smuggling goods between worlds and manipulation of nobles shown as clever.
Profit and trading are the premise; AniList ranks the Economics tag highest; MangaUpdates lists merchants and trading.

dominant: Pragmatism; market self-reliance; consumer goods as power

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Mitsuha talks her way into a lord's household rather than fighting, but later arms herself (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Self-directed entrepreneur working around rules of two worlds.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Driven by memory of her dead family, then by people around her shop.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Works within feudal nobility to gain status (ANN).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern goods, medicine and guns presented as superior to tradition (AniList tags).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Saving for retirement and financial security is the explicit goal.

folkways.japan: Reflects Japanese anxieties about retirement savings and the isekai convention of a modern Japanese person bringing knowledge to a premodern world.

delivery.evidence: ANN's review describes self-interest and ruthlessness through Mitsuha's choices, not lectures; no review calls it preachy.
delivery.note: The profit-minded outlook is carried by the heroine's schemes and is rarely challenged by another worldview in the sources.

winners_losers: Mitsuha prospers and rises in status; rivals and hostile forces lose to modern goods and weapons; pragmatic self-reliance gets the sympathy.
to_verify: No Wikipedia text in cache; war and gun violence detail rests on AniList tags (some marked spoilers) and one ANN volume-1 review.
